summary: This informational document provides a model of the information needed by the Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) process in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs). The model supports computing optical paths that obey constraints.

eli5.summary: Fiber cables carry many colors of light, and each path must use colors that work along the way. This note lists what facts a planner needs to know to pick paths and colors.

questions: information model for optical path computation
what is routing and wavelength assignment
what is a connectivity matrix in optical networks
subtitle: The facts a path planner needs about optical nodes and links to choose routes and wavelengths together.

tldr.problem: In a Wavelength Switched Optical Network a connection usually has to keep the same wavelength end to end, so computing a path means choosing the route and the wavelength together.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an information model of four categories (node, link, dynamic node and dynamic link information), written in RBNF, covering switch connectivity, converter pools, link properties and port wavelength restrictions.
tldr.outcome: It is a model, not an encoding. It leaves out optical impairments, and the actual protocol encodings are left to other documents.

today: RFC 7446 is an Informational document published in February 2015. The unit metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It builds on the framework in RFC 6163.

sections.title: Purpose of the Model
sections.content:
The model exists to support constrained optical path computation, not general network management. The constraint is often called wavelength continuity, and the resulting computation is the Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) problem. The model therefore carries enough topology, wavelength restriction and availability information for that computation.

It covers compatibility constraints between signals and network elements but not optical impairments. Parts of it are labelled "general" because they may also help other technologies that use a GMPLS control plane, while the rest is "WSON-specific". Terminology such as ROADM, WDM and wavelength conversion comes from RFC 6163.
sections.eli5: Picking a path in a light network means picking both the road and the color of light. This note lists what the planner has to know.

sections.title: Four Categories, Static and Dynamic
sections.content:
The model has four categories, regardless of whether data comes from a switching subsystem (such as a ROADM or OADM) or a line subsystem (such as WDM or an optical amplifier): Node Information, Link Information, Dynamic Node Information and Dynamic Link Information. This is roughly the categorization of ITU-T G.7715.

The split matters because some data changes with every connection setup or teardown, such as link wavelength usage, while other data is relatively static, such as port connectivity of a ROADM or channel spacing on a link. Keeping them apart allows separate updates, which reduces the processing and traffic load of distributing the dynamic data. The model is written in Routing Backus-Naur Form (RBNF).
sections.eli5: Some facts, like how a box is wired, almost never change. Others, like which colors are busy, change all the time, so they are kept in separate lists.

sections.title: Node Information
sections.content:
General node information contains the node identifier and connectivity matrices. A connectivity matrix is a conceptual M by N matrix, where M is the number of input ports and N the number of output ports. Matrix(i, j) is 0 or 1 depending on whether input port i can connect to output port j for one or more wavelengths. It shows potential connectivity only, not internal blocking. Its connection type is 0 for fixed and 1 for switched, and multiple matrices are allowed.

WSON-specific node information describes limited resources such as regenerators and wavelength converters. A resource block groups resources that behave identically. A resource pool is a collection of resource blocks that associates input ports with output ports through a block, and it can be modelled as a matrix. The model assumes N input fibers, P resource blocks and M output fibers. A pool input matrix RI(i,p) says whether input i can reach block p, a state vector RA(j) counts resources in use in block j, and an output matrix RE(p,k) says whether block p can reach output k. Static and dynamic wavelength constraints cover shared fibers.

Each resource block can also list input constraints, processing capabilities (number of resources, regeneration, fault and performance monitoring, vendor-specific) and output constraints. Optical interface classes and acceptable client signals (G-PIDs from RFC 3471 and RFC 4328) describe signal compatibility.
sections.eli5: For each box, the planner learns which doors connect to which, and which special color-changers sit inside and who can reach them.

sections.title: Link Information
sections.content:
Most static link data already exists in the GMPLS routing extensions for OSPF and IS-IS (RFC 4203, RFC 5307, RFC 5305). The model summarizes it and adds what WSONs need. Link information has a link ID plus optional elements:

  • Administrative group: configured bits that can influence routing decisions.
  • Interface switching capability descriptor: switching capabilities, combined in the OSPF and IS-IS extensions with maximum LSP bandwidth at eight priority levels.
  • Protection: what protection, if any, guards the link.
  • Shared Risk Link Group: links likely to fail together.
  • Traffic engineering metric: a data-channel metric separate from the control-plane path cost.
  • Port label restrictions: which wavelengths may or may not be used on a port.

These extras apply only to line-side ports of a WDM system or add/drop ports of a resource pool, not to tributary ports. Port label restrictions are the WSON-critical part. A "colored" ROADM drop port, for instance, has a channel count of one and a wavelength set of one member. The RFC also shows a ROADM built from splitters, combiners and WSSes with 11 output ports, where drop ports 1-4 share a constraint that a wavelength can be used only once across the group.
sections.eli5: For each pipe, the planner learns who owns it, whether it has a backup, which pipes break together, and which colors are allowed.

sections.title: Dynamic Information
sections.content:
Only a few elements change as connections come and go. For links, AvailableLabels is the set of wavelengths currently available. Combined with the port restrictions, it tells you which are in use. SharedBackupLabels is the set of wavelengths used for shared backup protection. For nodes, the only dynamic item is the resource pool state.

The model does not dictate encoding or placement. In some routing protocols the available label information may need to sit inside another element such as the Interface Switching Capability Descriptor, so each protocol's extensions should be consulted.
sections.eli5: The only things that keep changing are which colors are free right now and how many color-changers are busy.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The model is similar to what GMPLS routing protocols already convey: topology, link state and utilization, and switch and router capabilities. It should therefore be protected from disclosure to unintended recipients. Deliberate modification could significantly affect network operations, especially given the large capacity of optical infrastructure. A general discussion of security in GMPLS networks is in RFC 5920.
sections.eli5: This list tells an attacker a lot about the network, so it should be kept private and not tampered with.

items.title: Node Information
items.text: Relatively static: connectivity matrices and resource pools.

items.title: Link Information
items.text: Relatively static: protection, SRLG, metric and port label restrictions.

items.title: Dynamic Node Information
items.text: Resource pool state, such as resources in use.

items.title: Dynamic Link Information
items.text: Available labels (wavelengths) and shared backup labels.

viz.caption: WSON NODE INFORMATION IN RBNF, AS WRITTEN IN THE RFC

items.label: Simple label set
items.desc: Restricts a port to a given set of wavelengths.

items.label: Channel count
items.desc: Number of channels is at most MaxNumChannels.

items.label: Label range
items.desc: Restricts the range of labels that can be switched, such as a waveband device.

items.label: Combined
items.desc: Permitted labels plus a maximum number used at once.

items.label: Exclusivity
items.desc: A wavelength can be used at most once among a set of ports.
